# Datasets and Benchmarks

[Home](../../../README.md) · [All categories](../../README.md) · [简体中文](datasets_cn.md)

Manipulation Action Models → Gripper Manipulation Models → Datasets and Benchmarks

Reusable datasets, task environments and evaluation protocols for gripper manipulation, including single-arm, bimanual and mobile platforms. Use kind to distinguish datasets from benchmarks; record hardware, task coverage, paired cross-effector evidence and actual releases. Evaluating Coding Agents does not by itself make a benchmark an Agent Architecture; multiple robot platforms do not establish dexterous-hand validation. Retain the historical category code and catalog path.

| [AM.MAN.GRIP.1] <a id="am-man-grip-1"></a> | **TacClaw-Infinity｜Gripper demonstrations · Tactile dataset**<br>[TacClaw-Infinity: A Large-Scale Vision-Tactile-Language-Action Dataset for Dexterous Manipulation](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.20320v1)<br>Fucai Zhu et al<br>**Tags:** `dataset` `gripper` [tactile](../../topics/tactile.md) `umi` `robot-free-collection` `bimanual` `structured-annotation` `cross-embodiment` `real-world` | **Type:** Primarily a VTLA dataset, with a tactile UMI-style collection interface and processing methods.<br>**Construction:** Record synchronized vision, touch and end-effector motion without the target robot, with language descriptions; curate trajectories and annotate contact phases, subtasks and target objects.<br>**Scale/release:** Paper reports 10,000+ hours, 1M+ episodes and 1,000+ task types. The official portal advertises an initial 1,000-hour subset; replay/kinematic tools are public, while policy training/evaluation code is forthcoming.<br>**Evaluation scope:** TacClaw is a handheld gripper interface, not an articulated multi-finger hand. Two policies, π0.5 and StarVLA, are tested on three bimanual tasks across Tianji Marvin M6S Lite, RealMan RM75-b and DM-Sparky One, using 1,600 demonstrations and 50 trials per task. Collection scale is not the number of deployed evaluation tasks. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.20320v1) · [Project](https://daimon-robotics.github.io/tacclaw-infinity-page/) · [Code](https://github.com/daimon-robotics/TacClaw-Infinity) · [Data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/daimonrobotics/Daimon-Infinity) · [Notes](../../../notes/tacclaw-infinity.md) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-21 |
| [AM.MAN.GRIP.BENCH.1] <a id="am-man-grip-bench-1"></a> | **CaP-X｜Coding Agent · Primitive-level benchmarking · Code-generation post-training**<br>[CaP-X: A Framework for Benchmarking and Improving Coding Agents for Robot Manipulation](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.22435v2)<br>Letian Fu, Justin Yu, Karim El-Refai, Ethan Kou, Haoru Xue, Huang Huang, Wenli Xiao, Guanzhi Wang, Dantong Niu, Fei-Fei Li, Guanya Shi, Jiajun Wu, Shankar Sastry, Yuke Zhu, Ken Goldberg, Linxi “Jim” Fan<br>**Tags:** `benchmark` `gripper` `bimanual` `mobile-manipulation` `coding-agent` `agent-architecture` `code-as-policy` `code-generation` `tool-use` `primitive-abstraction` `multi-turn-interaction` `visual-differencing` `execution-feedback` `skill-library-synthesis` `candidate-code-ensemble` [reinforcement-learning](../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) `grpo` `code-generation-post-training` `sim-to-real` `simulation` `real-world` | **Hands:** Gripper-oriented control in core Robosuite single/bimanual tasks and LIBERO-PRO; extended BEHAVIOR evaluation uses mobile R1Pro, with Franka Panda and AgiBot G1 real-robot demonstrations. Interfaces chiefly expose gripper opening/closing; multi-finger dexterous joint-control evaluation was not found. Robot count is not hand-type count.<br>**Tasks:** V2 reports 187 CaP-Gym tasks: 7 Robosuite, 130 LIBERO-PRO and 50 BEHAVIOR. Core CaP-Bench compares 12 models across eight S1–S4/M1–M4 tiers, with 100 trials per task/tier on cube lift, stack, spill wipe, peg insertion, cube restack, two-arm lift and handover. Agent0 extends evaluation to 30 LIBERO-PRO and two BEHAVIOR tasks, the latter with 25 trials each. CaP-RL trains lift/stack/wipe separately; real-robot quantitative evaluation covers lift/stack with 25 trials each.<br>**Same-task cross-hand reuse:** Shared code interfaces support demonstrations across robots and sim-to-real, but no same-task transfer between grippers and multi-finger hands is validated. Single-to-bimanual deployment still changes control primitives; arbitrary effector deployment without adaptation and paired cross-hand evaluation are not established.<br>**Release:** The official MIT repository provides environment adapters, evaluation configurations, Agent0 and GRPO training/deployment instructions. V2 reports 187 tasks while the README still lists 39 alongside extension guides, so full released coverage is not independently verified. Some assets/perception models require upstream access. Separate demonstration datasets and post-trained checkpoint downloads remain unverified; local checkpoint-saving instructions do not prove released weights.<br>**Key distinction:** Controlled comparisons of primitive abstraction, single/multi-turn interaction and visual grounding separate Coding Agent capability from designer scaffolding. Visual-change text, synthesized helpers and candidate-code synthesis form training-free Agent0; simulation rewards additionally post-train a code generator.<br>**Evaluation scope:** The execution chain is task/observations → Python → perception, planning/IK and gripper APIs → feedback; controllers realize motions. Fixed-weight Agent0 reuses nine helpers synthesized once from successful traces, not demonstrated continual skill evolution. CaP-RL independently updates Qwen2.5-Coder-7B code generation per task with GRPO and privileged state APIs; deployed programs still call shared control tools, rather than a joint-level residual policy. Real lift/stack success is 84%/76% over 25 trials each, not an all-task or cross-hand result. | arXiv v2 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.22435v2) · [Project](https://capgym.github.io/) · [Code](https://github.com/capgym/cap-x) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-28 |
